task_instance: Create a minimal Packer HCL template (null source builder, no cloud creds needed) with an hcp_packer_registry block per the skill's example, run `packer init`/`packer validate` to confirm the config is well-formed, then run `packer build .` to actually push build metadata to the HCP Packer registry.
blocker_detail: The skill's core deliverable is pushing build metadata to HashiCorp's hosted HCP Packer registry via the hcp_packer_registry build block. Packer itself installs and runs fine, and the template (with hcp_packer_registry, bucket_labels, build_labels) validates successfully. But actually executing the push requires an HCP account and a service-principal's HCP_CLIENT_ID/HCP_CLIENT_SECRET/HCP_ORGANIZATION_ID/HCP_PROJECT_ID for HashiCorp's paid/account-bound cloud service (HCP). Running `packer build .` without these fails immediately with 'Error: HCP authentication information required'. Per sandbox safety rules, obtaining or using such account credentials for an external account-bound service is out of scope, so the push itself cannot be completed or verified in this runtime.
evidence: Downloaded and installed Packer 1.11.2 via curl from releases.hashicorp.com (no package manager needed) into the work dir; `./packer version` -> 'Packer v1.11.2'. Wrote /tmp/.../work/build.pkr.hcl containing a `source "null" "example"` build with an `hcp_packer_registry` block (bucket_name, description, bucket_labels, build_labels) exactly matching the skill's documented schema. `./packer init .` ran cleanly (no plugins required for null source). `./packer validate .` -> 'The configuration is valid.' Then `./packer build .` (with HCP_CLIENT_ID/SECRET/ORGANIZATION_ID/PROJECT_ID unset) -> 'Error: HCP authentication information required / The client authentication requires both HCP_CLIENT_ID and HCP_CLIENT_SECRET environment variables to be set for authenticating with HCP.' This is the exact blocker: the deliverable (a real push of build metadata into an HCP Packer registry bucket, then visible via `data.hcp_packer_artifact` in Terraform) requires a live HCP account and service-principal secret, which the sandbox rules forbid acquiring/using.
